prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: c024's criticality-aware area repair is the strongest independent mechanism (score +0.715, robust +0.211) and c026's tighter criticality shrink (6.0) slightly diluted it on ariane133; reverting the shrink coefficient to the c024 value of 3.0 while keeping the density cap from c021 should recover robustness across all three cases.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.574 robust(mean-std)=+0.188 min_case=+0.188 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.196 dWNS=+13.5% dTNS=+24.0% overflow~117
  bp-ng45: score=+0.188 dWNS=+13.5% dTNS=+22.6% overflow~96
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.190 dWNS=+20.3% dTNS=+18.0% overflow~175
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: reverting the shrink coefficient to 3.0 while keeping c021's density cap recovered robustness across all three cases (total +0.574, robust +0.188, all valid). Gains are consistent—dWNS +13.5–20.3%, dTNS +18–24%—with bp_fe-ng45 showing the largest WNS improvement, consistent with criticality-aware repair no longer being diluted. Overflow remains moderate (~96–175). Next step: sweep the shrink coefficient between 3.0 and 6.0 (e.g., 4.0–5.0) to confirm 3.0 is optimal rather than merely better than 6.0, and check overflow headroom on bp_fe-ng45.
